newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares leap 4.3 pct on new govt hopes.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares leap 4.3 pct on new govt hopes.

text.p: Istanbul shares soared on Monday morning in continued active buying amid hopes that a planned secularist alliance can win a confidence vote in parliament in coming weeks, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 ended the morning session 78 points, or 4.3 percent higher at 1,893 after brushing a trading record of 1,910. It had soared 10.5 percent last week to close at an all-time high of 1,815 on Friday.
Morning volume further rose to 31.92 trillion lira from Friday's 28.69 trillion.
Prime minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz met President Suleyman Demirel to ask him to approve his planned anti-Islamist government on Monday.

Yilmaz is due to hold a press conference er in parliament to announce his cabinet after getting Demirel's approval. The new government will face a vote of confidence in parliament in the next few weeks.

Yilmaz, the main conservative opposition leader, says Demirel has told him he would approve the government, set up to prevent the Islamists of outgoing caretaker Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan from returning to power.

"There was activity in most of the shares with strong financial structure and major impact on the market index. The upward move is likely to continue until the confidence vote. I expect the index to target 2,000 levels this week," said Toygar Sungur from Meksa securities.

Of the 246 shares traded, risers outdid losers sharply by 220 to 12 and 14 closed stable. The IMKB Industrial jumped 3.43 percent to 1,750, the IMKB Services surged 4.43 percent to 1,934 and the IMKB Financial soared 5.3 percent to 2,046.

Top actives were again led by bluechips -- largely state-owned flat steel maker Eregli, up 750 lira at 24,750, utilities Aktas Elektrik, up 10,000 lira at 255,000 and Cukurova Elektrik, up 15,000 lira at 270,000.
